name: sqstd_formaterrortracestring
note: Push `trace` (the captured async-fault trace array) rendered as a string (SQ_ERROR when it is not an array / has no frames).

name: sqstd_formaterrorcontextstring
note: Push the live callstack if it has frames, else `trace` (the async fault's captured trace array) rendered as a string. SQ_ERROR if neither is available: `trace` is null/not-an-array and there is no live callstack.

name: bind
note: Install the async runtime into the VM's shared state and build the Future class. The class is cached internally, embedders publish it where they want via future_push_class() or via SqModules::registerAsyncLib() / sqasync_register().  Call bind once per shared state, before any async function runs. A second call returns SQ_ERROR and asserts in dev builds.

name: pump
note: Drain the inbox + internal step queue. Call once per host frame, or in a drain loop on shutdown. The per-call cap bounds latency under reentrant scheduling (a callback that posts another callback). Returns the number of callbacks invoked - a zero return is not necessarily side-effect-free: a pump with an empty queue may still report previously deferred unhandled async faults through the VM error handler before returning.

name: has_pending
note: True iff the runtime has work it can drive forward on its own (queue or inbox non-empty, or a deferred unhandled-fault sweep is pending). Live tasks parked on a never-settling Future are NOT pending: they cannot advance without external input. Drain loops should OR this with their other pending-work signals (timer queues, in-flight HTTP, ...).

name: post_on_vm_thread
note: Schedule fn(user) to run on the VM thread inside the next pump(). VM-thread-only fast path. Returns SQ_ERROR if the runtime is not bound or is shutting down; on failure the caller owns `user` and must free it.

name: post_from_any_thread
note: Thread-safe variant of post_on_vm_thread: any thread may call. Returns SQ_ERROR if the runtime is not bound or is shutting down; on failure the caller owns `user` and must free it.

name: future_push_class
note: Push the cached Future class onto the stack. Fails if bind() has not been called. Useful for embedders that need to instantiate a Future from the C side (e.g. an async.delay native that returns one).

name: future_create
note: Create a fresh Future instance and write an addref'd handle into *out. Nothing is left on the stack. Caller owns one strong ref and must either settle the future via future_resolve/future_throw + sq_release, or release directly. Returns SQ_ERROR (raised) if the runtime is not bound or instance creation fails; `*out` is null on error.

name: future_resolve
note: Settle a Future from C. An internal sq_addref keeps the payload alive. Settling an already-settled future is a no-op.  The value is stored verbatim: a Future `value` is NOT unwrapped (await unwraps one level on the script side). future_throw faults the future with the value verbatim. Prefer routing documented failures as resolved values; reserve future_throw for worker-thread bugs with no live Quirrel stack to sq_throwerror into.  Both return SQ_ERROR and throw if `future` is not a Future instance or is a task-future. The only cycle guard is a direct self-settle (future_resolve(f, f) / future_throw(f, f)), which throws.

name: sqasync_register
note: SqModules RegFunc-shaped entry point. On entry the new module table is on top of the stack; the function adds "Future" -> class into it and leaves the table on top. Suitable for SqModules::registerStdLibNativeModule and SqModules::registerAsyncLib.
